cat > /app/submit/README.md <<'EOF'
# IPv6 sparse-node codec: compile + lookup pipeline

`run` is the entry point.  It reads one JSON request per line on stdin and
writes exactly one JSON response per line on stdout.

* `pipeline.py` – request validation, canonical IPv6 rendering, the
  deterministic sparse-node layout, exact rational peak minimisation over all
  legal cut vectors, image validation and longest-prefix-match lookup.
* `ftab.c` – optional native helper that computes the exact stage-usage table
  `F[b][e]` (the bit cost of a stage covering the interval `(b, e]`) with one
  bottom-up pass over the prefix trie.  It is compiled on demand into a
  temporary directory; if no compiler is available the equivalent pure Python
  implementation inside `pipeline.py` is used instead, so the behaviour is
  identical either way.

The stage usage of a cut pair depends only on that pair and on the FIB, so the
placement problem is a chain dynamic program: `F[b][e]` is computed once and
the peak utilisation `max_i U[i]/capacities[i]` is minimised exactly with
integer arithmetic scaled by `lcm(capacities)`.
EOF
